title: Anthropic contracts (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Anthropic contracts (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All contracts, agreements, licenses, subscriptions, task orders, delivery orders, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), memoranda of agreement (MOAs), letters of intent, data-sharing agreements, pilot or proof-of-concept agreements, statements of work, scopes of work, modifications, and other agreement documents between your agency and Anthropic PBC (including any subsidiary, affiliate, or successor entity), or its authorized resellers or cloud distributors acting on Anthropic's behalf (including, but not limited to, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Palantir Technologies, and Deloitte), that were active or entered into at any time between January 1, 2023, and the date of your search.

These records include, but are not limited to, any agreements relating to Anthropic's Claude products, including Claude, Claude for Enterprise, and Claude for Government, including under GSA's OneGov initiative or GSA Multiple Award Schedule contracts, and any agreements for access to, deployment of, or evaluation of Anthropic's models or services.

For each responsive contract or agreement, I request all documents attached or incorporated by reference, including pricing schedules, usage terms, data protection or data retention terms, acceptable-use or safety restrictions, service-level agreements, security requirements, and any related option or renewal periods.

I also request all records of communications between agency personnel and representatives of Anthropic PBC or its authorized resellers concerning the negotiation, evaluation, pricing, or terms of any such agreement, in any format in which they exist, including email, text messages, and messages on messaging platforms.

If complete contracts are voluminous, I ask that the agency, at minimum, produce:

A list or index of all responsive contracts and agreements, including contract or agreement number, vendor, contracting office, date, period of performance, and dollar value; and
The non-exempt portions of each contract, with redactions limited to the minimum necessary and accompanied by a description of the exemption applied.

Even where an exemption properly applies to part of a record, the statute requires release of all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. If any document is denied in part or in whole, please specify which exemption(s) are claimed for each passage or whole document denied, and provide a Vaughn index and an itemized inventory of withheld material, specifying the number of pages in each document and the total number of pages pertaining to this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Edmonds School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Baltimore Police Department)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Baltimore Police Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Baltimore Police Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Baltimore Police Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Baltimore Police Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Baltimore Police Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Baltimore Police Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Baltimore Police Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Baltimore Police Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Baltimore Police Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Baltimore Police Department or by third party who make the information available to Baltimore Police Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Baltimore Police Department’s jurisdiction.
